# NIST PQC Standardization Status

Covers the NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography standardization competition, selected
algorithms, and current standard designations. See [citations.md](../citations.md)
for full source details.

## Competition Timeline

| Date | Milestone |
|------|-----------|
| 2016 | Competition announced at PQCrypto 2016, call for proposals December 2016 [9] |
| End of 2017 | Submission deadline; 69 complete submissions received (23 signature, 59 KEM/PKE) [9] |
| January 30, 2019 | Round 2 candidates announced [9] |
| July 22, 2020 | Round 3 candidates announced [9] |
| July 5, 2022 | 4 algorithms selected for standardization; 4 KEMs advanced to Round 4 [2] |
| August 5, 2022 | SIKE broken by Castryck-Decru attack, removed from Round 4 [9][26] |
| August 13, 2024 | FIPS 203, 204, 205 published as final standards [1] |
| March 11, 2025 | HQC selected as fifth algorithm (backup KEM) [3] |

## Finalized Standards (August 13, 2024)

| Standard | Algorithm | Original Name | Purpose |
|----------|-----------|---------------|---------|
| FIPS 203 | ML-KEM | CRYSTALS-Kyber | Key encapsulation — protecting information over public networks [1] |
| FIPS 204 | ML-DSA | CRYSTALS-Dilithium | Digital signatures — primary method for authentication [1] |
| FIPS 205 | SLH-DSA | SPHINCS+ | Digital signatures — backup using different math than ML-DSA [1] |

NIST described the effort as an eight-year development program and stated that
quantum computing poses a threat potentially "within a decade" [1].

## Standards In Development

### FIPS 206 — FN-DSA (based on FALCON)

Draft submitted August 28, 2025. Expected publication late 2026 or early 2027 [1].
FN-DSA stands for "FFT (Fast-Fourier Transform) over NTRU-Lattice-Based Digital
Signature Algorithm" [9]. Key challenge: floating-point arithmetic creates
validation complexities across platforms.

### HQC Standard (FIPS number TBD)

Selected March 11, 2025 [3]. Code-based KEM using error-correcting codes, chosen
as backup to ML-KEM because it uses "fundamentally different mathematics" —
Dustin Moody (NIST): "We want to have a backup standard that is based on a
different math approach than ML-KEM" [3]. Draft standard expected ~2026, 90-day
public comment period, final standard 2027 [3].

## Round 4 Resolution

Four KEMs entered Round 4 in July 2022 [2]:

| Algorithm | Basis | Outcome |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| HQC | Code-based | Selected for standardization (March 2025) [3] |
| BIKE | Code-based | Not selected — security analysis less mature than HQC [46] |
| Classic McEliece | Code-based | Standardization delayed pending ISO coordination [46] |
| SIKE | Isogeny-based | Broken August 2022, removed [9][26] |

## Additional Digital Signatures Process

A separate call for additional digital signature algorithms was issued in summer
2022, with a June 1, 2023 submission deadline [2]. 40 complete submissions were
received. Round 2 announced October 24, 2024 with 14 candidates [9]. Round 2
estimated at 12-18 months, Round 3 planned for 2026.

## Algorithm Deprecation Timeline (NIST IR 8547)

NIST IR 8547 (Initial Public Draft, November 12, 2024) establishes the transition
roadmap [12]:

- **By 2030:** Algorithms at ≤112-bit security (RSA-2048, ECC P-256) deprecated [12][22]
- **By 2035:** All quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms disallowed [12][22]

## Gaps and Limitations

- FIPS 206 (FN-DSA) timeline is an estimate; floating-point determinism challenges
  may cause delays
- Classic McEliece NIST standardization depends on ISO coordination with no firm date
- NIST IR 8547 was an Initial Public Draft; final version may adjust dates
- Additional signatures Round 2 is ongoing; no final selections expected before 2026-2027
